zones.label: Clear Agreement
zones.summary: Clear consent is voluntary, specific, and comfortable.
facts: A genuine yes is free from pressure.
Agreement to one activity is not automatic agreement to another.
Body language and words should both indicate comfort.

zones.label: Checking In
zones.summary: Consent is ongoing, so respectful people check in as circumstances change.
facts: Ask a clear question and leave room for any answer.
A check-in is meaningful only when no is safe to say.

zones.label: Uncertainty
zones.summary: Unclear, hesitant, frozen, or mixed responses mean stop.
facts: Do not guess or treat silence as yes.
Make space, reduce pressure, and ask once respectfully.
If clarity does not come, the activity does not continue.

zones.label: Withdrawal
zones.summary: A person can change their mind and withdraw consent at any time.
facts: Changing one’s mind is not wrongdoing.
Respectful response protects safety and trust.

zones.label: Coercion
zones.summary: Threats, guilt, persistence, secrecy, or power pressure invalidate consent.
facts: Coercion can be verbal, social, digital, or connected to authority.
A person experiencing coercion is not to blame.
